extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook section covering tensor products of algebras, flatness (definitions, criteria, and Lazard's theorem), Cayley–Hamilton and Nakayama lemmas, integrality/module-finiteness and normalization, and localization with universal properties. Intended as reference/lecture notes for learning/proving results in commutative algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of R-algebras is an R-algebra / coproduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Given R-algebras S and T with structure maps R -> S and R -> T, the tensor product U := S ⊗_R T is an R-algebra with product defined on pure tensors by (s⊗t)(s'⊗t') = ss'⊗tt'. Moreover, S ⊗_R T satisfies the universal mapping property (UMP) making it the coproduct of S and T in the category of R-algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes construction of canonical maps S -> S⊗_R T and T -> S⊗_R T, and the bijection Hom_R-alg(S⊗_R T, V) ≅ Hom_R-alg(S,V) × Hom_R-alg(T,V) for any R-algebra V. Example: S⊗_R R[X1,...,Xn] ≅ S[X1,...,Xn].

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical isomorphism S ⊗_R R[X1,...,Xn] = S[X1,...,Xn]
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-algebra S and variables X1,...,Xn, there is a canonical S-algebra isomorphism S ⊗_R R[X1,...,Xn] ≅ S[X1,...,Xn].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by showing both algebras satisfy the same universal mapping property for S-algebra homomorphisms determined by images of Xi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact functor and left/right exact definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor F between module categories is exact if it preserves exact sequences; left exact if it preserves kernels (and, for contravariant functors, if it takes cokernels to kernels); right exact if it preserves cokernels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Hom(P, -) is exact iff P is projective; Hom(N, -) and Hom(-, N) are left exact; - ⊗ M is right exact. Precise equivalences about preserving short exact sequences, kernels+surjections, cokernels+injections, etc., are given in Proposition (9.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of exactness for R-linear functors (Prop 9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-linear functor F between module categories, the following are equivalent: (1) F preserves all exact sequences; (2) F preserves short exact sequences; (3) F preserves kernels and surjections; (4) F preserves cokernels and injections; (5) F preserves kernels and images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outlines how each condition implies others using standard homological diagram chases and the snake lemma. Use this to check exactness by verifying simpler properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of flat module
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module M is flat (over R) if the functor - ⊗_R M preserves injections (equivalently, is exact since ⊗ is always right exact). An R-algebra R' is flat over R if R' is flat as an R-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the working definition used to derive many equivalent criteria (Lazard, ideal/equational criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct sum flatness criterion (Lemma 9.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct sum ⊕_i M_i is flat if and only if each summand M_i is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces injectivity of tensor maps on the sum to injectivity on each summand using properties of tensor and direct sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free and projective modules are flat (Prop 9.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every free R-module is flat; every projective R-module is flat (projective modules are direct summands of free modules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that R is flat over itself and that direct summands inherit flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfully flat equivalences (Exercise 9.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-algebra R' is faithfully flat over R iff the canonical map M -> M ⊗_R R' is injective for every R-module M. Equivalent conditions include: (2) φ(1)·(aR') = a for every ideal a of R; (3) Spec(R') -> Spec(R) is surjective; (4) for every maximal ideal m of R, mR' ≠ R'; (5) for any nonzero R-module M, M ⊗_R R' ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalences give practical tests for faithful flatness and relate algebraic and geometric criteria (surjectivity on spectra).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness along short exact sequences with flat terms (Prop 9.12(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 is exact and M'' is flat, then for any module N the sequence 0 -> M' ⊗ N -> M ⊗ N -> M'' ⊗ N -> 0 is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses chosen projective presentation of N and snake lemma; standard method to propagate exactness when tensoring with flat modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-out-of-three for flatness in short exact sequences (Prop 9.12(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In a short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 with M'' flat, M is flat iff M' is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses tensoring with arbitrary injective maps and diagram chases; useful to build flat modules from known ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered direct limits of flat modules are flat (Prop 9.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: A filtered direct limit (colimit) lim_i M_i of flat modules M_i is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that tensor commutes with filtered colimits and injectivity is preserved in the colimit; foundational for Lazard's theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom-tensor canonical map and finiteness criteria (Prop 9.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a canonical map Hom_R(M,N) ⊗_{R'} P -> Hom_R(M, N ⊗_{R'} P) when N is an (R,R')-bimodule and P an R'-module. If P is flat and M is finitely generated, the map is injective; if M is finitely presented, the map is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed via Watts's theorem or explicit bilinear formulas. Use presentations of M to reduce to the free case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-change map Hom_R(M,N) ⊗_R R' -> Hom_{R'}(M⊗_R R', N⊗_R R') (Ex 9.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a canonical base-change map; if R' is flat over R and M is finitely generated then the map is injective, and if M is finitely presented it is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard base-change properties for Hom under flat extensions; used to control Hom after tensoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category C_M and presentation of module as colimit (Def 9.16 & Prop 9.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a module M, define category C_M of maps R^m -> M; the forgetful functor yields M ≅ colim_{(R^m -> M) in C_M} R^m. In other words, M is the filtered colimit of finite free modules mapping to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presentation is used in Lazard's theorem to express flat modules as filtered colimits of finite free modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lazard's Theorem: characterizations of flat modules (Thm 9.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-module M the following are equivalent: (1) M is flat; (2) for every finitely presented P, the map Hom_R(P,R) ⊗_R M -> Hom_R(P,M) is surjective; (3) every map P -> M from finitely presented P factors through some R^n -> M; (4)-(6) various finite relation/factorization formulations; (7) the category C_M is filtered; (8) M is a filtered direct limit of finite-rank free modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem gives both conceptual and practical criteria (presentations, relations) and is the principal structural characterization of flat modules in commutative algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equational criterion for flatness (Ex 9.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flatness can be tested by relations: given a relation Σ_i x_i y_i = 0 (x_i in R, y_i in M), there exist x_{ij} in R and y'_j in M such that y_i = Σ_j x_{ij} y'_j for all i and Σ_i x_i x_{ij} = 0 for all j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reformulation (from Lazard's equivalent conditions) is often used to check flatness by rewriting relations in 'matrix' form; it's the practical 'equational' test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal criterion for flatness (Lemma 9.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module N is flat iff for every finitely generated ideal a of R the natural map a ⊗_R N -> aN (multiplication) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof shows the ideal criterion is equivalent to the equational criterion and is often used as a convenient sufficient and necessary test, especially with finitely generated ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: fraction field is flat over a domain (Ex 9.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a domain and K = Frac(R), then K is flat over R (indeed a ⊗_R K = K for any ideal a) but K is not projective unless R = K (i.e., R is a field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates that flatness is weaker than projectivity; useful counterexamples for intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat modules over domains are torsion-free; converse for PID (Ex 9.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a domain and M is flat, then M is torsion-free (multiplication by nonzero x is injective). Conversely, if R is a PID and M is torsion-free then M is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives simple checks for flatness in the PID/domain context; used frequently in examples and classification over PIDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant Trick / Cayley–Hamilton (Thm 10.2 and 10.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finitely generated module M generated by m1,...,mn and an endomorphism φ with matrix (a_{ij}) relative to those generators, the characteristic polynomial p_M(T) = det(TI - (a_{ij})) satisfies p_M(φ) = 0 in End(M). This yields the classical Cayley–Hamilton theorem for matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via forming the matrix ∆ with entries δ_{ij}φ - (multiplication by a_{ij}) and multiplying by the vector of generators, then using adjugate/cofactor matrix to deduce p_M(φ)=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion M = aM iff (1+a)M = 0 for some a in a (Prop 10.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finitely generated module M and ideal a, M = aM iff there exists an element a ∈ a such that (1 + a)M = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Cayley–Hamilton applied to the matrix of coefficients expressing generators in terms of the ideal to produce such an element; conversely, (1+a)M=0 implies M=aM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjective endomorphism on a finitely generated module is an isomorphism (Cor 10.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated and φ: M -> M is surjective, then φ is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses polynomial action of φ to show M = X·M in P=R[X], apply previous proposition to deduce a relation giving inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of rank and free generating sets (Cor 10.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any n generators of the free module R^n form a basis (are free) and if R^m ≅ R^n then m = n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from the previous corollary by constructing the endomorphism taking standard basis to given generators and showing it is invertible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama's Lemma (Lemma 10.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a ring and m ⊆ rad(R) an ideal. If M is finitely generated and M = mM then M = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Proposition 10.3 to find a ∈ m with (1+a)M = 0 and that 1+a is a unit, or minimal generating set argument; fundamental lemma in local algebra for detecting vanishing/generators modulo maximal ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Nakayama on generators mod m (Prop 10.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If M/N is finitely generated and N + mM = M then N = M. (2) For finitely generated M, elements m1,...,mn generate M iff their images generate M/mM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard corollaries giving tests for generation and lifting bases from residue fields in local rings; used to define minimal generating sets and rank invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences for finite projective/free/flat modules (Prop 10.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-module P: (1) P free of finite rank implies (2) P projective and finitely generated, implies (3) P flat and finitely presented. If R is local, all three conditions are equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses splitting of presentations and Nakayama's lemma in the local case; gives criteria relating projectivity, flatness, finite presentation and freeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module-finite algebra and integrality (Def 10.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-algebra R' is module-finite over R if R' is a finitely generated R-module. An element x ∈ R' is integral over R if it satisfies a monic polynomial xn + a1 xn-1 + ... + an = 0 with ai ∈ R. R' is integral over R if every element is integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrality is equivalent to module-finiteness of R[x] as an R-module for single elements; forms the basis for normalization and integral extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent tests for integrality of an element (Prop 10.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For x ∈ R': (1) x satisfies a monic equation of degree n; (2) R[x] is generated as R-module by 1,x,...,x^{n-1}; (3) x lies in a subalgebra generated as an R-module by n elements; (4) there exists a faithful R[x]-module M generated over R by n elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proves equivalence to module-finiteness conditions and gives practical ways to verify integrality (via finite generation or existence of faithful finite modules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monic generator of ideal in polynomial ring <=> free quotient of rank n (Cor 10.20)
rubrics_metrics.description:
For P = R[X] and ideal a in P with R' = P/a and x the image of X: a =

with p monic of degree n iff 1,x,...,x^{n-1} form a free basis of R' over R iff R' is free of rank n over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects algebraic property of the defining polynomial with module-theoretic freeness; useful in constructing finite free algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely generated modules over module-finite algebras are finitely generated over base (Lemma 10.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R' is module-finite over R and M is finitely generated as R'-module, then M is finitely generated as R-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by expressing generators of R' and M and taking their products; used in transitivity arguments for module-finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tower law for integrality (Thm 10.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If x ∈ R'' is integral over R' and R' is integral over R then x is integral over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by building intermediate subrings and using module-finiteness transitivity (Lemma 10.21) and characterization (Prop 10.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences: finitely generated algebra integral ⇔ module-finite (Thm 10.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an R-algebra R', the following are equivalent: (1) R' is finitely generated as an algebra and integral over R; (2) R' = R[x1,...,xn] with each xi integral over R; (3) R' is module-finite over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that integrality + finite algebra generation is equivalent to finite R-module generation; practical criterion for recognizing integral extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral closure / normalization (Def 10.25 & Cor 10.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The integral closure (normalization) of R in R' is the subring of elements of R' integral over R. The integral closure is an R-algebra and is integrally closed in R'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: integral closure is closed under addition/multiplication by using module-finiteness of generated subrings; used to define 'normal' rings when R = integral closure in Frac(R).

rubrics_metrics.name: UFD implies normal (Gauss Thm 10.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a unique factorization domain (UFD) then R is integrally closed in its fraction field (i.e., normal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by writing fraction in lowest terms r/s and showing that integrality forces s to be a unit; fundamental structural fact about UFDs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization construction and equivalence relation (Def 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring R and multiplicative subset S, define equivalence (x,s) ~ (y,t) if there exists u ∈ S with xtu = ysu. The localization S^{-1}R is the set of equivalence classes with operations (x/s)+(y/t)=(tx+sy)/st and (x/s)(y/t)=xy/st. The map φ_S: R -> S^{-1}R sends x to x/1 and sends elements of S to units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives concrete construction and algebraic rules; establishes basic properties including when localization is zero (iff S contains a nilpotent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total quotient ring as localization at nonzerodivisors (Ex 11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is the set of nonzerodivisors of R then S^{-1}R is called the total quotient ring, and the natural map R -> S^{-1}R is injective. For domains this recovers the field of fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to embed rings into their total quotient ring and to study denominators in general rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal mapping property of localization (Thm 11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: S^{-1}R is universal among R-algebras in which every element of S becomes a unit: given φ: R -> R' a ring map, φ(S) ⊆ R'^× iff there exists a unique map S^{-1}R -> R' with composition φ_S -> S^{-1}R -> R' equal to φ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This UMP characterizes localization categorically and is the standard tool for constructing maps out of localizations and proving uniqueness of such maps.
